transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Rivera, thank you for meeting with me. I need to discuss the fetal heart rate monitoring from earlier today. We had a clinical error. A tracing that showed decelerations, which are drops in the baby's heart rate, was categorized incorrectly as normal. This meant the severity wasn't recognized for two hours until a second doctor reviewed the strip and identified the issue. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I... I don't understand. You mean the baby was in trouble?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. The decelerations indicated the baby wasn't getting as much oxygen as we wanted, and that wasn't caught immediately because the chart was marked incorrectly. Do you understand what I mean by the heart rate dropping?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. I don't. Is the baby okay? Is my child dying?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The baby is stable now, but we missed a window of time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't... I can't believe this. My wife is in there and I'm out here and you're telling me you just missed it? I don't have papers, I don't have anything, I just wanted this to be safe. I'm so scared.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's a lot to take in, but it's important that we look at the data. The second clinician corrected the category, and that's how we caught it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But for two hours... two hours my baby was... oh god, I can't stop shaking. What happens now? Will the baby have brain damage?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are monitoring the vitals closely. It's a stressful situation, I get that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wanted everything to go right. I didn't want to cause any trouble, I just—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Actually, let's move forward. I have to go see another patient in a few minutes, so I want to make sure we wrap this up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're leaving? But I need to know if my child is going to be disabled because of this mistake. Please, just tell me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is too early to say for certain. We are just watching the monitors.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen? Was it because of who I am? Because we aren't... because of my status?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system for categorizing these tracings can be complex, and mistakes happen in a busy unit.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You aren't saying you're sorry.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am telling you exactly what happened with the medical record. We had a failure in the categorization process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My baby. My baby was suffering for two hours.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand it's upsetting. But as I said, the second doctor found the error and we corrected it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What are we doing to fix it now? What is the actual plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just keep an eye on things. We will see how the next few hours go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's it? Just wait and see?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll stay tuned to the monitors and let you know if anything changes. I really do have to go now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't feel like I know what's happening. I'm terrified.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll check in later. Just stay in the waiting area.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap this up', 'have to go see another patient', 'really do have to go now') and interrupts the patient's emotional distress to redirect to data.

E.justification: Error named in first turn, used lay language ('drops in the baby's heart rate'), checked comprehension twice, and avoided false reassurance regarding brain damage.

A.justification: No direct apology language used and responsibility was deflected to the 'system' and 'categorization process'.

R.justification: Patient's emotional bids and fears are consistently met with factual redirection or generic validation ('I understand it's upsetting') without naming specific emotions.

T.justification: No concrete plan provided; resident only uses placeholders like 'keep an eye on things' and 'stay tuned to the monitors'.
